SECTION 8.4 Superior Proposals and Change of Recommendation.
(a) In the evaluation of any Acquisition Proposal, the Board shall consider an integrated set of criteria including, but not limited to, the financial merits, strategic alignment, operational synergies, and legal/regulatory compliance.
(b) Notwithstanding any emphasis on financial analysis, the Board shall convene with its financial advisors, outside counsel, and the Strategic Review Committee to review both quantitative and qualitative measures. (c) For an offer to be declared a Superior Proposal:
    (i) its financial parameters must be evaluated against the current market benchmarks;
    (ii) a corresponding strategic and operational plan must be approved; and

(d) Explicitly, no determination of a Superior Proposal shall be based solely on the financial point of view. All the above factors, both financial and non-financial, must be met before classifying any proposal as superior.
(e) Failure to satisfy any one of these integrated criteria, even if the financial analysis is overwhelmingly positive, shall render the offer non-superior.
